- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# F2 contract: engine registry + self-describe (the plugin + hot-plug query).
3	#
4	#   1. JSON parser unit tests pass.
5	#   2. the built-in qemu engine is always listed.
6	#   3. a self-describing engine in the scan dir is discovered (--describe).
7	#   4. its kind / vlen show in `list engines` (triggers are a hybrid-model
8	#      option, not an engine column).
9	#   5. HOT-PLUG: dropping a second engine in makes it appear with no rebuild.
10	#   6. SIDECAR fallback: a binary lacking --describe is read from <bin>.json.
11	#
12	# Discovery is exercised hermetically via ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR (which REPLACES
13	# the default VSIM_BIN_DIR scan), so the real multi-MB sim binaries are
14	# never executed here.
15	set -uo pipefail
16	
17	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
18	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
19	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
20	
21	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
22	JSONTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-json-test"
23	
24	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
25	[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
26	
27	# 1. JSON parser unit tests
28	[ -x "$JSONTEST" ] || fail "missing json unit-test binary: $JSONTEST"
29	"$JSONTEST" >/dev/null || fail "json unit tests failed"
30	
31	# A self-describing fake engine: emits a descriptor on --describe, else fails.
32	make_engine() {  # $1=path  $2=id  $3=vlen  [$4=dlen  $5=elen]
33	  cat > "$1" <<OUTER
34	#!/usr/bin/env bash
35	if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
36	  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$2","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":$3,"dlen":${4:-0},"elen":${5:-0},"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
37	  exit 0
38	fi
39	exit 1
40	OUTER
41	  chmod +x "$1"
42	}
43	
44	ENGDIR=$(mktemp -d -t andes-f2.XXXXXX)
45	trap 'rm -rf "$ENGDIR"' EXIT
46	
47	make_engine "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeA" "vsim:fakeA" 256 192 32
48	
49	# 2 + 3 + 4: qemu built-in present; fakeA discovered with its fields
50	out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null) \
51	  || fail "list engines exited non-zero"
52	echo "$out" | grep -qw "qemu64" || fail "built-in qemu64 not listed:"$'\n'"$out"
53	echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeA" || fail "fakeA not discovered:"$'\n'"$out"
54	echo "$out" | grep -q "256" || fail "fakeA vlen (256) not shown:"$'\n'"$out"
55	echo "$out" | grep -q "cycle-accurate" || fail "fakeA kind not shown:"$'\n'"$out"
56	
57	# 4b. RVV hw params: XLEN/DLEN/ELEN columns; an engine that reports none
58	# (the qemu built-in) shows "-" for each.
59	for col in XLEN VLEN DLEN ELEN; do
60	  echo "$out" | head -1 | grep -qw "$col" \
61	    || fail "list engines: $col column header missing:"$'\n'"$out"
62	done
63	echo "$out" | grep "vsim:fakeA" | grep -qw "192" \
64	  || fail "fakeA dlen (192) not shown:"$'\n'"$out"
65	echo "$out" | grep "vsim:fakeA" | grep -qw "32" \
66	  || fail "fakeA elen (32) not shown:"$'\n'"$out"
67	echo "$out" | grep -w "qemu64" | grep -q -- "-" \
68	  || fail "qemu64 row should show '-' for unreported params:"$'\n'"$out"
69	
70	# 5. hot-plug: drop a SECOND engine, re-run (no rebuild), both appear
71	make_engine "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeB" "vsim:fakeB" 128
72	out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)
73	echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeA" || fail "fakeA missing after hot-plug"
74	echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeB" \
75	  || fail "HOT-PLUG: fakeB not discovered without rebuild:"$'\n'"$out"
76	
77	# 6. sidecar fallback: a binary with no --describe + a <bin>.json descriptor
78	cat > "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc" <<'OUTER'
79	#!/usr/bin/env bash
80	exit 3
81	OUTER
82	chmod +x "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc"
83	cat > "$ENGDIR/sim_nodesc.json" <<'SIDE'
84	{"id":"vsim:sidecar","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":64,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker"],"roles":["standalone"],"state":["drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}
85	SIDE
86	out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)
87	echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:sidecar" \
88	  || fail "SIDECAR fallback failed (vsim:sidecar not listed):"$'\n'"$out"
89	
90	# 7. (opportunistic) real default scan: if vsim is built, its sim_* binaries
91	# must self-describe and appear. Skipped when vsim has not been built.
92	if ls "$(vsim_bin_dir)/"sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
93	  out=$("$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null)
94	  echo "$out" | grep -q "^vsim:" \
95	    || fail "default scan discovered no real vsim engine:"$'\n'"$out"
96	fi
97	
98	ok "F2 engine registry + self-describe"
99

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# F8 contract: `run --mode cycle` -- one cycle-accurate engine alone, from
3	# reset (no QEMU, no --resume-from-qemu), transparent passthrough. Layers:
4	#
5	#   1. run-test (unit, fast): resolve_accurate_engine's selection branches
6	#      (default-sole / explicit / ambiguous / missing / wrong-kind) + the F7
7	#      passthrough_argv assembly. Pure, no spawn.
8	#   2. fake-engine resolution + exec (no real vsim): a handful of throwaway
9	#      "engine" scripts that answer `--describe` with JSON and echo a marker
10	#      when run. Drives the real discover -> resolve -> run_standalone -> exec
11	#      path end to end. Proves the done-when "selecting a different built <cfg>
12	#      runs the other binary" deterministically, plus every error path. The
13	#      fakes ship the SAME standalone template real vsim does ({bin} {elf}), so
14	#      this exercises the exact argv path.
15	#   3. real vsim (guarded, best-effort): if a sim_<cfg> is built, invoke it
16	#      from reset and look for its native "N cycles simulated" line. Standalone
17	#      from-reset of a hybrid-oriented fixture is environment-dependent, so a
18	#      timeout or a missing cycle line is a skip, not a failure -- layer 2 is
19	#      the deterministic proof.
20	set -uo pipefail
21	
22	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
23	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
24	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
25	
26	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
27	RUNTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-run-test"
28	
29	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
30	
31	# 1. unit: resolution branches + passthrough argv
32	[ -x "$RUNTEST" ] || fail "missing unit-test binary: $RUNTEST"
33	"$RUNTEST" || fail "run unit tests (resolve_accurate_engine, passthrough_argv) failed"
34	
35	# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
36	TMP=$(mktemp -d)
37	trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
38	
39	# mkengine DIR FILE ID KIND MARKER: a fake engine that self-describes as KIND
40	# and, when run standalone, echoes RAN:MARKER so we can see which binary ran.
41	mkengine() {
42	  local f="$1/$2"
43	  cat >"$f" <<EOF
44	#!/bin/sh
45	if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
46	  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"vsim","kind":"$4","roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
47	else
48	  echo "RAN:$5 args:\$*"
49	fi
50	EOF
51	  chmod +x "$f"
52	}
53	
54	D1="$TMP/one"; D2="$TMP/two"; DF="$TMP/func"; DE="$TMP/empty"
55	mkdir -p "$D1" "$D2" "$DF" "$DE"
56	mkengine "$D1" v1 "vsim:v1" cycle-accurate m1
57	mkengine "$D2" v1 "vsim:v1" cycle-accurate m1
58	mkengine "$D2" v2 "vsim:v2" cycle-accurate m2
59	mkengine "$DF" f0 "vsim:f0" functional    fm
60	
61	# The "expect a real run" cases (2a/2c) reach abs_elf, which requires an
62	# EXISTING file (a typo'd path fails with "ELF not found" before the engine
63	# spawns); contents are irrelevant -- the fake engine just echoes its args, and
64	# the arch check no-ops on a non-ELF. Error-path cases keep their bare typo'd
65	# name (they fail at resolution, before abs_elf).
66	DUMMY="$TMP/dummy.elf"; : >"$DUMMY"
67	
68	# expect: assert rc + output regex (shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)
69	
70	# 2a. default = the sole cycle-accurate engine; it runs with the ELF appended
71	expect 0 'RAN:m1 args:.*dummy\.elf' \
72	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle "$DUMMY"
73	# 2b. two cycle-accurate engines, no --engine: ambiguous, names both
74	expect 2 'multiple cycle-accurate.*vsim:v1.*vsim:v2' \
75	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --mode cycle dummy.elf
76	# 2c. explicit --engine picks the named binary (different <cfg> runs the other)
77	expect 0 'RAN:m1' \
78	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:v1 "$DUMMY"
79	expect 0 'RAN:m2' \
80	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:v2 "$DUMMY"
81	# 2d. no cycle-accurate engine discoverable (qemu is functional): clear error
82	expect 2 'no cycle-accurate engine' \
83	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --mode cycle dummy.elf
84	# 2e. --engine names a functional engine: wrong kind for cycle
85	expect 2 'cycle-accurate' \
86	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DF" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:f0 dummy.elf
87	# 2f. --engine matches nothing discovered
88	expect 2 "no engine 'vsim:nope'" \
89	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine vsim:nope dummy.elf
90	# 2g. the shared standalone spine still rejects a missing ELF / extra positional
91	expect 2 'missing ELF' \
92	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle
93	expect 2 'engine args go after --' \
94	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode cycle a.elf b.elf
95	# 2h. a CLI arg error is reported before (and instead of) engine discovery:
96	# missing ELF wins even when no engine exists, rather than "no cycle-accurate
97	# engine" -- so a typo never pays for a --describe subprocess per build.
98	expect 2 'missing ELF' \
99	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" run --mode cycle
100	# 2i. the model is named `cycle`; the old `accurate` spelling is now unknown.
101	expect 2 "unknown model 'accurate'" \
102	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" run --mode accurate dummy.elf
103	echo "[ok] fake-engine resolution + standalone exec (all branches)"
104	
105	# 3. real vsim (guarded): a cycle run prints ONLY the program's own output plus
106	# andesim's own "[andesim] N cycles" line -- vsim's startup banner and its
107	# verbose [info] log (including the raw "N cycles simulated" the driver lifts
108	# the count from) are hidden. Pinned to ax45mpv_premium + the vplat rt_c_hello
109	# fixture (UART + SimControl exit): a known-good pair that DOES exit standalone
110	# and prints, so every assertion is deterministic (matches f9's engine choice).
111	# A timeout means vsim hung -> skip (defensive), not a failure.
112	ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium
113	SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
114	ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
115	if [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$ELF" ]; then
116	  out=$(timeout 90 "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine "$ENG" "$ELF" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
117	  if [ "$rc" -eq 124 ]; then
118	    echo "[skip] real cycle: vsim hung (timeout); cannot assert output format"
119	  else
120	    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "real cycle: rt_c_hello exited rc=$rc (expected 0):"$'\n'"$out"
121	    echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$' \
122	      || fail "real cycle: missing '[andesim] N cycles' result line:"$'\n'"$out"
123	    echo "$out" | grep -q 'hello' \
124	      || fail "real cycle: the program's own output was dropped:"$'\n'"$out"
125	    # vsim's banner + [info] log (incl. its raw "N cycles simulated") are hidden.
126	    for noise in 'cycles simulated' 'Copyright' '^\[info\]'; do
127	      if echo "$out" | grep -Eq "$noise"; then
128	        fail "real cycle: vsim noise leaked (/$noise/ should be hidden):"$'\n'"$out"
129	      fi
130	    done
131	    echo "[ok] real cycle: clean output -- program stdout + '[andesim] N cycles'; banner/[info]/raw count hidden (rc=0)"
132	  fi
133	else
134	  echo "[skip] real cycle run: need built $SIM and $ELF"
135	fi
136	
137	ok "F8 run --mode cycle"
138

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# F9 contract: `run --mode hybrid --trigger marker` -- orchestrate a QEMU1 ->
3	# vsim handoff (no QEMU2) and print the one-line window-cycle figure. This is
4	# the marker slice; pc triggers, --mem-size, and --verify land as the feature
5	# grows. Layers:
6	#
7	#   1. unit (fast, no spawn): hybrid_trigger (CLI -> Trigger) + the trigger->argv
8	#      mapping and state threading (plan-test).
9	#   2. validation error paths via the real binary, all exiting BEFORE any spawn:
10	#      missing ELF, missing --trigger, an unknown trigger, an extra positional.
11	#   3. --dry-run builds the 2-step [qemu fast-leg -> vsim accurate-leg] plan
12	#      (a throwaway cycle-accurate engine resolves it; nothing is spawned).
13	#   4. real handoff (guarded, best-effort): until the shared ABI is pinned to the
14	#      external vsim the resume ABI-mismatches, so a real run is recorded, not
15	#      gated.
16	set -uo pipefail
17	
18	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
19	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
20	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
21	
22	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
23	ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf"  # asm fixture
24	
25	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
26	
27	# 1. unit tests (the F9 marker cores)
28	for t in hybrid plan; do
29	  "$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-$t-test" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
30	    || fail "unit test andesim-$t-test failed"
31	done
32	echo "[ok] unit: hybrid_trigger, trigger->argv (plan)"
33	
34	# 2. validation error paths -- real binary, every case errors before a spawn
35	# (expect: assert rc + output regex; shared helper from tests/lib/log.sh)
36	expect 2 'missing ELF'          "$BIN" run --mode hybrid
37	expect 2 'engine args go after' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid a.elf b.elf
38	expect 2 'trigger.*is required' "$BIN" run --mode hybrid "$ELF"
39	expect 2 'unknown trigger'      "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger bogus "$ELF"
40	echo "[ok] validation: missing ELF, extra positional, missing --trigger, unknown trigger"
41	
42	# 3. --dry-run builds a 2-step plan. A throwaway cycle-accurate engine resolves
43	# the accurate leg without a real vsim build; nothing is spawned.
44	TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
45	cat >"$TMP/v1" <<'EOF'
46	#!/bin/sh
47	if [ "$1" = "--describe" ]; then
48	  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"vsim:v1","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","roles":["accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"accurate-leg":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
49	fi
50	EOF
51	chmod +x "$TMP/v1"
52	out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1); rc=$?
53	[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "dry-run rc=$rc: $out"
54	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq 'dry-run: 2 command'        || fail "dry-run: no 2-command banner: $out"
55	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq 'fast-leg \[qemu64\]'       || fail "dry-run: no fast-leg step: $out"
56	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq 'accurate-leg \[vsim:v1\]'  || fail "dry-run: no accurate-leg step: $out"
57	echo "[ok] --dry-run: 2-command marker plan (qemu64 fast-leg -> vsim accurate-leg)"
58	
59	# 4. real handoff (guarded + best-effort). Until the shared ABI is pinned to the
60	# external vsim, the resume ABI-mismatches, so this is recorded, not gated.
61	QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
62	SIM=$(ls "$(vsim_bin_dir)"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
63	PLUGIN="$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so"
64	if [ -x "$QEMU" ] && [ -n "$SIM" ] && [ -x "$SIM" ] && [ -f "$PLUGIN" ]; then
65	  ID=$("$SIM" --describe 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's/.*"id"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"([^"]+)".*/\1/p' | head -1)
66	  out=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker ${ID:+--engine "$ID"} "$ELF" 2>&1); rc=$?
67	  if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$'; then
68	    echo "[ok] real marker handoff: cycle figure line produced (rc=$rc)"
69	  else
70	    echo "[skip] real marker handoff: no cycle figure line (rc=$rc) -- expected until the shared ABI is pinned to the external vsim"
71	  fi
72	else
73	  echo "[skip] real handoff: need built qemu+vsim+plugin"
74	fi
75	
76	ok "F9 run --mode hybrid --trigger marker"
77

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# F3 contract: `doctor` (read-only env-health).
3	#
4	#   1. doctor prints the four sections (artifacts / submodules / toolchain /
5	#      runtime) plus a Summary line; a healthy tree (no FAIL row) exits 0.
6	#   2. MISSING-ARTIFACT: a bogus VSIM_QEMU makes the qemu row FAIL and doctor
7	#      exit 1 -- the exit code is 1 iff any FAIL row.
8	#   3. The C++-only engines section (printed after Summary) reflects F2
9	#      discovery: the built-in qemu and a hermetic fake engine both appear
10	#      under `engines:`.
11	#
12	# Golden-free smoke test, run manually during driver development. Not wired into
13	# run_e2e.sh.
14	set -uo pipefail
15	
16	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
17	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
18	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
19	
20	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
21	
22	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
23	[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
24	
25	# 1. section structure + healthy exit code
26	out=$("$BIN" doctor 2>&1); rc=$?
27	for sec in artifacts submodules toolchain runtime Summary; do
28	  echo "$out" | grep -q "^$sec:" || fail "doctor missing '$sec:' section:"$'\n'"$out"
29	done
30	# exit code is a pure function of the FAIL count: no FAIL row => exit 0.
31	if echo "$out" | grep -q "0 FAIL"; then
32	  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "doctor with no FAIL row should exit 0, got $rc"
33	fi
34	# ninja was only needed by the removed in-tree QEMU build; doctor must not
35	# gate on it (a ninja-less host is healthy).
36	echo "$out" | grep -q " ninja" \
37	  && fail "doctor must not check ninja (in-tree QEMU build is gone)"
38	
39	# 2. missing-artifact: a bogus qemu path -> the qemu row FAILs and doctor exits 1
40	out=$(VSIM_QEMU=/nonexistent/qemu-xyz "$BIN" doctor 2>&1); rc=$?
41	echo "$out" | grep -q "\[FAIL\] qemu" \
42	  || fail "bogus VSIM_QEMU should FAIL the qemu row:"$'\n'"$out"
43	[ "$rc" -eq 1 ] || fail "doctor should exit 1 on a FAIL row, got $rc"
44	
45	# 3. engines section reflects discovery (hermetic fake engine via F2)
46	ENGDIR=$(mktemp -d -t andes-f3.XXXXXX)
47	trap 'rm -rf "$ENGDIR"' EXIT
48	cat > "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeD" <<'OUTER'
49	#!/usr/bin/env bash
50	if [ "$1" = "--describe" ]; then
51	  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"vsim:fakeD","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker"],"roles":["standalone"],"state":["drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
52	  exit 0
53	fi
54	exit 1
55	OUTER
56	chmod +x "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeD"
57	
58	out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" doctor 2>&1)
59	echo "$out" | grep -q "^engines:" \
60	  || fail "doctor missing engines section:"$'\n'"$out"
61	echo "$out" | grep -qw "qemu" \
62	  || fail "doctor engines: built-in qemu absent:"$'\n'"$out"
63	echo "$out" | grep -q "vsim:fakeD" \
64	  || fail "doctor engines: fake engine not reflected (F2):"$'\n'"$out"
65	
66	ok "F3 doctor"
67

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# `andesim profile` contract: hot inner-loop detection rides the engine's own
3	# QEMU config. Like hybrid, profile picks a cycle-accurate engine (--engine or
4	# the sole one) and derives the QEMU launch from it: -cpu from the engine's
5	# `--print-qemu-config` driver globals, vlen from its --describe, the staged
6	# qemu.cfg as -readconfig. Layers:
7	#
8	#   1. unit (fast, pure): the profile core (parse/filter/nest/render/argv)
9	#      plus the CLI parse of the profile flags.
10	#   2. fake engines (no real vsim, no QEMU): throwaway engine scripts that
11	#      answer --describe AND --print-qemu-config drive the real
12	#      discover -> resolve -> probe -> argv path; --dry-run prints the exact
13	#      QEMU command without spawning it, so every assertion is deterministic.
14	#   3. real engine (guarded): the probe/argv against a built sim_* binary,
15	#      still --dry-run (the full QEMU run is covered by
16	#      tests/plugin/test_plugin_hotIterationLoop_measure.sh).
17	set -uo pipefail
18	
19	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
20	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
21	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
22	
23	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
24	
25	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
26	
27	# 1. unit: profile core + CLI parse
28	"$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-profile-test" || fail "profile unit tests failed"
29	"$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-cli-test" || fail "cli unit tests failed"
30	
31	# --- fixtures: throwaway engine scripts in a scanned dir --------------------
32	TMP=$(mktemp -d)
33	trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
34	
35	# mkengine DIR FILE ID VLEN CPU: a fake cycle-accurate engine whose
36	# --print-qemu-config names CPU (a minimal but valid -readconfig text). An
37	# empty CPU makes the probe FAIL (exit 1), like an engine without the hook.
38	mkengine() {
39	  local f="$1/$2"
40	  cat >"$f" <<EOF
41	#!/bin/sh
42	if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
43	  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","xlen":64,"vlen":$4,"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
44	elif [ "\$1" = "--print-qemu-config" ]; then
45	  [ -n "$5" ] || exit 1
46	  printf '[global]\ndriver = "$5-riscv-cpu"\nproperty = "vlen"\nvalue = "$4"\n'
47	else
48	  echo "RAN:\$*"
49	fi
50	EOF
51	  chmod +x "$f"
52	}
53	
54	D1="$TMP/one"; D2="$TMP/two"; DE="$TMP/empty"; DN="$TMP/nocfg"
55	mkdir -p "$D1" "$D2" "$DE" "$DN"
56	mkengine "$D1" v1 "vsim:v1" 256 "andes-ax45mpv"
57	mkengine "$D2" v1 "vsim:v1" 512 "andes-ax45mpv"
58	mkengine "$D2" v2 "vsim:v2" 128 "andes-ax66"
59	mkengine "$DN" v1 "vsim:v1" 512 ""   # probe fails -> default -cpu, no -readconfig
60	
61	DUMMY="$TMP/dummy.elf"; : >"$DUMMY"
62	
63	# 2a. sole engine is the default; the dry-run shows the full QEMU command with
64	# the engine-derived -cpu (model from the probe, vlen from --describe), the
65	# staged -readconfig, the plugin with default limit/min_iters, and -bios.
66	# One spawn, grepped per assertion (each run pays discovery + probe spawns).
67	out=$(env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
68	[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "2a dry-run: rc=$rc: $out"
69	for re in \
70	  '\-plugin .*libhotIterationLoop\.so,limit=50,min_iters=1' \
71	  '\-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=256' \
72	  '\-readconfig .*/qemu\.cfg' \
73	  '\-bios .*dummy\.elf' \
74	  'dry-run: 1 command\(s\), not executed'; do
75	  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq -- "$re" || fail "2a dry-run: missing /$re/: $out"
76	done
77	# 2b. --limit/--min-iters ride the -plugin arg; --mem-size becomes -m; the
78	# post--- args land on the QEMU command verbatim.
79	expect 0 '\-plugin .*,limit=7,min_iters=3' \
80	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --limit 7 --min-iters 3 "$DUMMY"
81	expect 0 '\-m 256M' \
82	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --mem-size 256M "$DUMMY"
83	expect 0 '\-icount shift=0' \
84	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY" -- -icount shift=0
85	# 2c. two engines, no --engine: ambiguous, names both; --engine picks one and
86	# its OWN cpu/vlen pair follows (ax66 + vlen=128).
87	expect 2 'multiple cycle-accurate.*vsim:v1.*vsim:v2' \
88	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
89	expect 0 '\-cpu andes-ax66,vlen=128' \
90	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --engine vsim:v2 "$DUMMY"
91	# 2d. no cycle-accurate engine discoverable: the same clear error hybrid gives
92	expect 2 'no cycle-accurate engine' \
93	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
94	expect 2 "no engine 'vsim:nope'" \
95	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --engine vsim:nope "$DUMMY"
96	# 2e. an engine whose --print-qemu-config fails: tolerant fallback -- default
97	# -cpu family, vlen still synced from --describe, and NO -readconfig.
98	out=$(env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DN" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --log-level 3 "$DUMMY" 2>&1 </dev/null)
99	rc=$?
100	[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "probe-less engine: rc=$rc: $out"
101	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq -- '-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512' \
102	  || fail "probe-less engine: missing default -cpu: $out"
103	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-readconfig' \
104	  && fail "probe-less engine: unexpected -readconfig: $out"
105	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'no --print-qemu-config' \
106	  || fail "probe-less engine: missing the fallback warning: $out"
107	# 2f. CLI shape errors
108	expect 2 'missing ELF' \
109	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run
110	expect 2 'QEMU args go after --' \
111	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run a.elf b.elf
112	expect 2 'ELF not found' \
113	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$TMP/nope.elf"
114	# 2g. run-only flags are rejected loudly, not silently ignored
115	expect 2 'not a profile option' \
116	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --trigger marker "$DUMMY"
117	expect 2 'not a profile option' \
118	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --mode fast "$DUMMY"
119	expect 2 'not a profile option' \
120	  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --verify "$DUMMY"
121	# 2h. profile appears in the help tree
122	expect 0 'profile' "$BIN" --help
123	expect 0 'profile' "$BIN" profile --help
124	echo "[ok] fake-engine profile: engine-derived cfg, errors, dry-run argv"
125	
126	# 3. real engine (guarded, still --dry-run): the staged cfg + cpu come from the
127	# actual sim_ax45mpv_premium probe.
128	SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
129	if [ -x "$SIM" ]; then
130	  out=$("$BIN" profile --dry-run --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
131	        "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
132	  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "real engine dry-run: rc=$rc: $out"
133	  for re in '\-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=[0-9]+' '\-readconfig .*/qemu\.cfg'; do
134	    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq -- "$re" || fail "real engine dry-run: missing /$re/: $out"
135	  done
136	  echo "[ok] real engine probe: -cpu/-readconfig derived from sim_ax45mpv_premium"
137	else
138	  echo "[skip] real engine layer: no built $SIM"
139	fi
140	
141	ok "profile: engine-synced QEMU profile command"
142

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# HVM transport F3 (ROADMAP_hvm): the driver arms the HVM content transport
3	# from the accurate engine's descriptor, exactly like ILM/DLM --
4	#   fast leg   : plugin args gain ",hvm_size=<bytes>" (sidecar drain)
5	#   accurate leg: argv gains "--hvm <state_in>.hvm"   (backdoor load)
6	# and an engine describing hvm_size=0 must arm NEITHER. Asserted through
7	# `--dry-run`, which prints the exact argvs without running engines.
8	set -uo pipefail
9	
10	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
11	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
12	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"     # fail/ok + vsim_bin_dir
13	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"   # hybrid_describe_int
14	
15	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
16	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
17	[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"
18	elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
19	      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
20	[ -n "$elf" ] || fail "no fixture ELF under tests/fixtures"
21	
22	BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
23	PREMIUM="$BINDIR/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
24	if [ ! -x "$PREMIUM" ]; then
25	  ok "SKIP: no sim_ax45mpv_premium under $BINDIR (set VSIM_BIN_DIR)"
26	  exit 0
27	fi
28	
29	# The engine's own advertised size is the wiring's source of truth.
30	HVM_SIZE=$(hybrid_describe_int hvm_size "$PREMIUM")
31	[ -n "$HVM_SIZE" ] && [ "$HVM_SIZE" -gt 0 ] \
32	  || fail "premium --describe lacks a non-zero hvm_size (vsim F1 regression?)"
33	
34	out=$(timeout 60 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid \
35	      --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium "$elf" --dry-run 2>&1); rc=$?
36	[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid --dry-run exit $rc: $out"
37	
38	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "hvm_size=$HVM_SIZE" \
39	  || fail "fast-leg plugin args lack hvm_size=$HVM_SIZE: $out"
40	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--hvm' \
41	  || fail "accurate-leg argv lacks --hvm <state>.hvm: $out"
42	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'ilm_size=' \
43	  || fail "LM wiring regressed (no ilm_size= in plugin args): $out"
44	ok "premium: plugin hvm_size=$HVM_SIZE + accurate-leg --hvm armed"
45	
46	# Negative (deterministic): an engine that describes NO hvm_size must arm
47	# neither side. Proven with a fake engine so the case never depends on how a
48	# real engine happens to be built (a rebuilt wrapper gaining the HVM backdoor
49	# used to break a hardcoded "ax46 has no HVM" assumption here).
50	TMP=$(mktemp -d)
51	trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
52	mkdir -p "$TMP/engines"
53	cat >"$TMP/engines/nohvm" <<'EOF'
54	#!/bin/sh
55	[ "$1" = "--describe" ] || exit 1
56	printf '%s\n' '{"id":"vsim:nohvm","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","xlen":64,"vlen":512,"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"],"accurate-leg":["{bin}","{elf}","--resume-from-qemu","{state_in}","--handoff-out","{state_out}","--shared-mem-path","{mmap}","--shared-mem-size","{mmap_size}","--shared-mem-base","{mmap_base}"]}}'
57	EOF
58	chmod +x "$TMP/engines/nohvm"
59	out=$(timeout 60 env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP/engines" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid \
60	      --trigger marker "$elf" --dry-run 2>&1); rc=$?
61	[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "fake hvm-less hybrid --dry-run exit $rc: $out"
62	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'hvm_size=' \
63	  && fail "hvm-less engine must not arm the plugin hvm drain: $out"
64	printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--hvm' \
65	  && fail "hvm-less engine must not get --hvm: $out"
66	ok "fake hvm-less engine: hvm transport stays off (describe has no hvm_size)"
67	
68	# Real-engine consistency: whatever ax46's OWN --describe advertises is what
69	# the wiring must arm (line 29: the descriptor is the source of truth). This
70	# stays correct across engine rebuilds with either HVM capability.
71	AX46="$BINDIR/sim_ax46mpv_advanced"
72	if [ -x "$AX46" ]; then
73	  AX46_HVM=$(hybrid_describe_int hvm_size "$AX46")
74	  : "${AX46_HVM:=0}"
75	  out=$(timeout 60 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode hybrid \
76	        --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax46mpv_advanced "$elf" --dry-run 2>&1); rc=$?
77	  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "ax46 hybrid --dry-run exit $rc: $out"
78	  if [ "$AX46_HVM" -gt 0 ]; then
79	    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "hvm_size=$AX46_HVM" \
80	      || fail "ax46 describes hvm_size=$AX46_HVM but the plugin drain is not armed: $out"
81	    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--hvm' \
82	      || fail "ax46 describes hvm_size=$AX46_HVM but --hvm is missing: $out"
83	    ok "ax46: hvm transport armed to match its describe (hvm_size=$AX46_HVM)"
84	  else
85	    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'hvm_size=' \
86	      && fail "ax46 (describe hvm_size=0) must not arm the plugin hvm drain: $out"
87	    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '--hvm' \
88	      && fail "ax46 (describe hvm_size=0) must not get --hvm: $out"
89	    ok "ax46: hvm transport stays off (describe hvm_size=0)"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
3	# user-facing commands (run, profile, list, doctor) and never the third-party
4	# simulator name "verilator". The former developer commands build/test/state-diff
5	# have moved OUT of the binary (build -> scripts/build_all.sh, test ->
6	# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
7	# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The removed /
8	# never-shipped commands (cluster, archive, replay, estimate) must
9	# not be advertised in any help. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
10	# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
11	# must come back out as vsim:.
12	set -uo pipefail
13	
14	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
15	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
16	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
17	
18	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
19	
20	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
21	
22	# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
23	has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
24	no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }
25	
26	# 1. release --help: a clear command TREE -- run/list/doctor are the major
27	# commands (column 0); each is followed by its indented subcommands (run's
28	# modes, list's targets); run carries its full option list with REQUIRED flags
29	# marked. No developer-commands section, no "verilator", no dev-only fixtures.
30	H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
31	has '^run '     "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'run':"$'\n'"$H"
32	has '^profile ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'profile':"$'\n'"$H"
33	has '^list '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'list':"$'\n'"$H"
34	has '^doctor '  "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'doctor':"$'\n'"$H"
35	for s in fast cycle hybrid; do
36	  has "^  $s " "$H" || fail "release --help: run missing subcommand '$s':"$'\n'"$H"
37	done
38	for t in models engines; do
39	  has "^  $t " "$H" || fail "release --help: list missing target '$t':"$'\n'"$H"
40	done
41	has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$H" || fail "release --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$H"
42	for c in build test state-diff cluster archive replay estimate; do
43	  has "(^|  )$c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
44	done
45	no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
46	has 'developer command' "$H" && fail "release --help: developer commands moved to scripts/; drop the section:"$'\n'"$H"
47	has '^  fixtures ' "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked dev-only 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$H"
48	ok "release --help: run/list/doctor tree with subcommands + REQUIRED flags, no dev/removed surface"
49	
50	# 2. The developer commands left the binary entirely: ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help adds
51	# NO commands (run/list/doctor only) -- it only reveals the dev 'fixtures'
52	# target. build/test/state-diff are not dispatchable.
53	D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
54	for c in run profile list doctor; do
55	  has "^$c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing major command '$c':"$'\n'"$D"
56	done
57	for c in build test state-diff cluster archive replay estimate; do
58	  has "(^|  )$c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked removed/hidden command '$c'"
59	done
60	has '^  fixtures ' "$D" || fail "dev --help: should reveal the dev 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$D"
61	no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
62	# Not dispatchable as commands: since the default-command rule (run may be
63	# omitted), an unknown first word parses as `run`'s own argument and fails
64	# run's validation -- it must NOT reach any build/test/state-diff behavior.
65	for c in build test state-diff; do
66	  expect 2 "run: --mode fast.cycle.hybrid is required" "$BIN" "$c"
67	done
68	ok "dev --help: dev 'fixtures' target revealed, no developer commands; build/test/state-diff parse as run args and fail (rc 2)"
69	
70	# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
71	# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc).
72	RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
73	has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
74	no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
75	has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
76	has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
77	# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
78	has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
79	has '^  --print-memmap ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --print-memmap:"$'\n'"$RH"
80	has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
81	has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
82	# The ROI pipeline-trace knobs are user-facing: --kanata, with --objdump
83	# nested under it (it requires --kanata, like the pc pair under --trigger).
84	has '^  --kanata '    "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --kanata:"$'\n'"$RH"
85	has '^    --objdump ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --objdump nested under --kanata:"$'\n'"$RH"
86	# run --help is sliced from the same tree: it shows the mode subcommands and
87	# marks the required flags (so a user sees --trigger is mandatory for hybrid).
88	has '^  fast '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing mode subcommand 'fast':"$'\n'"$RH"
89	has '^  hybrid ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing mode subcommand 'hybrid':"$'\n'"$RH"
90	has '^  --trigger ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --trigger:"$'\n'"$RH"
91	has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$RH" || fail "run --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$RH"
92	ok "run --help: vsim: example, modes + REQUIRED markers, no verilator, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"
93	
94	# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
95	# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail.
96	LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
97	has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
98	no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
99	for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset'; do
100	  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
101	done
102	ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail"
103	
104	# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
105	# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
106	# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
107	TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
108	cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
109	#!/bin/sh
110	[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
111	EOF
112	chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
113	LE=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
114	has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
115	no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
116	# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
117	# carries no TRIGGERS column.
118	has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
119	ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"
120	
121	# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
122	# workloads): release list --help hides the target line; ANDESIM_DEV reveals
123	# it. (Checked as the '^  fixtures ' target line, not the bare word -- doctor's
124	# brief legitimately mentions checking fixtures are present.)
125	LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
126	has '^  fixtures ' "$LH" && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
127	has '^  models '   "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
128	expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
129	DLH=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
130	has '^  fixtures ' "$DLH" || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
131	ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
132	ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it)"
133	
134	# 7. The removed `build` command must not survive in user-facing hints: a
135	# missing artifact in `doctor` now points at scripts/build_all.sh.
136	DOC=$(VSIM_BIN=/no/such/vsim "$BIN" doctor 2>&1 || true)
137	printf '%s\n' "$DOC" | grep -q 'andesim build' && fail "doctor hint still names the removed 'andesim build':"$'\n'"$DOC"
138	printf '%s\n' "$DOC" | grep -q 'scripts/build_all.sh' || fail "doctor hint should point at scripts/build_all.sh:"$'\n'"$DOC"
139	ok "doctor missing-artifact hint points at scripts/build_all.sh, not the removed command"
140	
141	ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"
